rows.why: Cory Klippsten states in his own voice why markets were selling, and the clip has no unresolved referents and nothing in the window retracts it. The title repeats the clip without strengthening it, and the neutral VO links imply no relation to Natalie Brunell's clip.

The host is reading Matt Cratter's tweet aloud to mock it ('I had it on good authority... Please advise Matt Cratter's tweet'), then ridicules it ('Where were those lawsuits?'), so this is not the speaker's own assertion. The title attributes the claim to BTC Sessions and drops the irony.

Cory Klippsten states this himself as his own analysis, backed by the broadband and railroad comparison, and nothing in the window retracts or conditions it. The title repeats the clip at the same certainty, and the neutral 'Over to Coin Bureau' bridge implies no reply or rebuttal between the two videos.

Jeff Booth is voicing the opposing view against himself ("Or you could argue on my side, he's delusional. This will never exist. It will always be captured."), not his own sincere assertion. In context he believes the reverse. The title presents the line as a flat claim from the show, which inverts the speaker's meaning.

In the clip Taylor is describing Big Tech's counterargument ('the counterargument in big tech is... we should be competing for the top engineer'), not stating her own view, and she then says she sees the other side. The title presents that line as Fox Business's own assertion, which reverses who holds the view.

The host sincerely states his own long-term thesis, and the clip itself resolves 'that' ('more and more people choosing to hold and use scarce money'), with nothing in the window retracting or qualifying it. The title quotes it faithfully, there are no time words, and the neutral VO bridge implies no reply or relation to the Coin Bureau price-recap clip.

In the moment clip Short describes what other people will say about Vance and immediately rejects it ('I think that's way premature'). The title 'He's Done' presents that view as the speaker's own assertion, reversing its polarity, and the referent 'he' (JD Vance) is never resolved in the package.

The clip's referents ('you can't' meaning hiding in one industry, 'they all' meaning sectors in a 2027 downturn) are only resolved in the preceding source lines, and the package never supplies them. Placing 'No, you can't' right after Melker's 'Doomers are usually wrong' also implies a rebuttal between two separate videos.

The clip is the host reading aloud a tweet from 'Dumerified', and moments later he refutes it, citing community notes that no outflows from Satoshi-attributed wallets have occurred since 2010. The title and package present the false claim as BTC Sessions' own assertion, reversing the speaker's meaning.

Joe Burnett states this as his own view, extending Jeff Booth's technology-deflation thesis to gold, and nothing in the window retracts it. The package attributes it only to 'Stephan Livera's show' (not to Livera himself), adds no thesis beyond the quote, uses no time words, and implies no relation to the Bitcoin Mechanic clip.

In the moment, Melker is paraphrasing the 'doomers' he argued against. He calls their claims bottom signals and says STRC is back at par. The title 'Scott Melker on Strategy: It Was Over' presents their view as his own sincere assertion, which reverses his meaning.

Mark Moss is answering a devil's-advocate question in his own voice, and the clip keeps both the condition (decentralized and secure) and his hedge ('I don't think'). The rest of the window reinforces rather than retracts it, and the neutral VO bridge and accurate title imply no relation to the Coin Bureau clip and add no thesis.

Lepard is mockingly voicing the complacent 'it's all under control' crowd and right after says 'I don't believe it.' The package presents 'sell your Bitcoin... because you don't need it' as his own sincere view, which reverses his meaning.

The 'it' in the clip refers to tokenized stocks becoming the main way things trade, and the claim depends on a condition stated outside the clip ('if in the next two years... the DTCC has tokenized stocks'). The package resolves neither, so in a Bitcoin show next to a Bitcoin clip, viewers would likely take it as an unconditional claim that Bitcoin can't be stopped.

The moment is Bitcoin Mechanic's own sincere conclusion, following from his argument that merchant and KYC restrictions change user behavior, and nothing later in the window retracts it. The title quotes him verbatim with correct attribution, and the neutral 'Also on the record' bridge implies no reply or rebuttal relation with Brunell's clip.

In the clip, "It" means paying through KYC-gated checkouts (X Premium, wallet apps) that strip out Bitcoin's peer-to-peer nature, and neither the clip nor the package resolves this. Placed right after Brunell's "Bitcoin imposes a global free market" and under the title, it reads as Bitcoin itself being pointless and as a rebuttal to her, which reverses his meaning and invents a dialogue between the two videos.

Lewis sincerely states that the 75K target held and Bitcoin made no new low after the election results; nothing in the window retracts or conditions this. The package keeps the clips separate with neutral VO, the title only restates the clip, and there is no time word to misdate.

The 'it' in the clip is Heatbit's Bitair air-purifier miner, which Busarov explicitly says is not about ROI, and the package never identifies it. Placed after a clip about investing in Bitcoin, viewers would read it as describing home or heat-reuse mining or Bitcoin generally, even though he says right after that his Bitwater product is about real economics.

The 'it' in Dave's line refers to a possible congressional testimony by Jensen Huang on Nvidia chips reaching China via Megaspeed. Neither the clip nor the package resolves this, and the statement depends on the condition 'if he does appear before the Senate and the House.' Placed after a Swan Bitcoin clip about the AI trade, viewers would likely misread what the line is about.

Joe Burnett sincerely describes what the stock-to-flow model charted. The referent is self-contained, nothing in the window retracts it, the package attributes it to Stephan Livera's show without misnaming the speaker, and the title restates what the clip says without implying a link to the Coin Bureau clip.

The clip is part of a hypothetical worked example ('for example, if you and I both buy one Bitcoin and Bitcoin goes to a million'), not a sincere assertion that Bitcoin will reach a million. The title presents it as a flat claim, adding certainty the speaker did not express, and it omits his caveat that not all treasury companies will outperform.

In context this is the guest's (Jeff Booth's) own sincere conclusion to his free-market argument, with no unresolved referents and nothing in the window retracting it. The package attributes it neutrally to the show, adds no thesis beyond the quote, and its neutral bridge to the Swan clip implies no reply or rebuttal.

The clip is the interviewer voicing a fear held by politicians, framed as a question to Lee, and Lee pushes back on it right afterward, saying the models won't be that 'big shiny' and Europe should build applications. The title attributes 'Europe is just late to the game' to Kai-Fu Lee, which gives the wrong speaker and reverses what he actually meant.

In context, the guest (apparently Armani Ferrante, answering the host) merely floats 'a political statement' as one possible reading and then rejects it ('I think it's just simple… it's a new thing'). The title presents it as a firm claim and attributes it to Scott Melker, the host, which flips both its meaning and its speaker.

The title 'Investors Will Dump AI Stocks for Bitcoin' adds a thesis no clip states. Klippsten only says investors are questioning AI returns, and that Bitcoin gets sold alongside stocks, so the title also reverses the polarity and overstates the certainty of what he meant.
